02 / The service

One identity across different vehicles.

Fleet graphics give vans, cars and commercial vehicles a recognisable identity across your business. Our Norwich team designs, produces and fits fleet graphics for companies running local service vehicles, delivery vans and mixed fleets across Norfolk. A rollout can start with a couple of vehicles or be spread over several fitting dates, depending on which vans need to stay on the road.

We start with a list of makes, models, model years and body sizes, then plan how your colours, logo and contact details will carry across them. What works on the long side of a Luton needs a different layout on a car door. A master design gives the fleet a shared look while proofs for each vehicle type show how it fits around doors, windows, trims and equipment.

Tell us which vehicles are being replaced first, where they are based and whether any already carry graphics. That helps us discuss removal, fitting batches and how new vehicles can match the approved artwork. If you run leased vehicles, include the handback requirements in the brief.

08 / Vinyl & materials

Choose the right film.

Specify film, finish and colour across the master design. Keep an approved print sample and note which vehicles use a different film because of panel shape, use or removal requirements.

Cast vs calendered
Cast vinyl conforms to more complex bodywork. Suitable calendered film can work on flatter areas and simpler curves. The exact product and surface determine suitability.
Brands used
3M and Metamark are examples to discuss. Ask for the product and finish on your quote.
Lifespan
Film, panel angle, care and exposure all matter. As one product example, 3M 2080 lists up to eight years on qualifying vertical applications and up to three on horizontal applications. Check the applicable product terms.
Finishes
Ask about gloss, matt, satin, chrome-effect or reflective film. Speciality finishes can have different fitting, care and durability requirements.

15 / FAQ

Fleet graphics Norwich: your questions.

What do you need to quote a fleet?

Send the vehicle count, makes and models, photos if available and any brand guidelines. Tell us which vehicles need graphics first.

Can you match our existing fleet graphics?

Share photos and any artwork you have. We can review how closely the layout and colours can be matched before you approve a design.

Can you start with a small fleet?

Yes. Give us the vehicle count and which ones need graphics first. The layout can be planned for future additions.

Do all vehicles need to be the same model?

No. We adapt the approved design to each body style and agree the placement on separate proofs where needed.

Can you fit in stages?

Tell us which vehicles are available and when. We can plan fitting dates around agreed batches at the Norwich workshop.

Can you match film already on our fleet?

Send the existing artwork, film references and recent photos. Ageing and weathering can change colour, so we discuss how closely new work can match.

What information do you need to price the fleet?

Send the vehicle count, makes, models, wheelbases or body sizes, photos and existing artwork. Mention removal work or special markings up front.

Can individual fleet numbers be included?

Yes. Include the number list and preferred positions in the brief so we can plan a consistent layout and check each proof.

How can I prepare for lease handback?

Check each vehicle’s terms and book removal in advance. Share the condition of the paint and any repairs so we can advise before fitting or removal.

Can you replace graphics on one damaged panel?

Send a photo of the damage and the original artwork if you have it. We can assess whether a panel replacement or a larger section is needed for a consistent finish.
